Chapter 7. The Power of Pausing: Creating Space for Choice.
Think about those moments when anger rushes in—everything feels so urgent, doesn’t it? Words just spill out, actions follow before you even realize, and regret usually shows up a little too late. But here’s something simple that can completely shift how things unfold: the pause.
Picture this—a teenager, totally fed up with their parent’s rules, just about to snap back. But then, right as the words are about to fly, they remember to pause. It’s only a few seconds—a breath, a heartbeat—but that tiny space changes everything. Suddenly, the urge to lash out softens, and there’s room for a new choice: to speak honestly, but without causing harm.
Pausing doesn’t mean you’re pushing anger down or pretending it’s not there. No, it’s about creating a gap between what you feel and how you react—a chance to really notice what’s going on inside. Most of us skip right past this moment, swept up by our old habits. But if you learn to pause, you find this hidden freedom—the freedom to choose how you want to respond.
Imagine a manager, blindsided by criticism in a meeting. Their old instinct? Defend, maybe even snap back. But this time, they pause. They draw a slow breath and notice that tightness in their chest. In this brief silence, they remember their goal: to listen and learn. The conversation moves forward, but now it’s less combative, more open.
Pausing can be as quick as a single breath, or as long as a walk around the block. What really matters is your willingness to stop, even for just a moment, and pay attention. It’s in that space you start to see anger for what it really is—a passing emotion, not a command you have to follow.
Think of a couple, caught in the middle of an argument. They both agree to take a break, head to different rooms, breathe, and reflect. When they come back together, the urgency is gone. Now, they can talk about what really matters, without anger taking over the conversation.
Remember, pausing is a practice—it’s not a magic fix you use once and never think about again. It takes patience, and a lot of self-compassion, especially when old habits are stubborn. But every time you pause, your mind gets a bit clearer, and your heart a little stronger.
Some people worry that pausing will make them look weak or indecisive. But honestly? It’s a sign of strength—choosing a wise response over just reacting on impulse. Over time, you’ll find the pause becomes a real ally, helping you bring more mindfulness and care to everything you do.
The real magic of pausing is in its simplicity. You don’t need any special skills or equipment—just the willingness to stop and notice. And in that small space, that’s where real transformation begins.
